human_tolerance.notes: Lives in parks and managed woodland near people (for example Phoenix Park, Dublin, and Epping Forest). The sources do not give suburban or urban density figures.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Southern Hemisphere rut begins in April; a rut lasts about 135 days, so the end is derived. Authored for AU only.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Derived: PanTHERIA gestation 230 days after April matings gives mid-November to December births. The window is authored.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Northern Hemisphere rut begins in the second half of October; the end is derived from the 135-day rut. Applies to the native range only.

vocalizations.description: Low-frequency groan made by males during the rut, produced by the shape of the oral and nasal vocal tract. Males also give high-pitched whines to start mating; only the groan is modelled.

taxonomy.note: GBIF usageKey 5220136 accepted at species rank (checked 2026-10-31). ITIS TSN 552472 valid, Dama dama (Linnaeus, 1758).

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 42161 is active, species rank; Wikidata P3151 = 42161 and P846 = 5220136. Wikidata Q159857 is the item for Dama dama.

common_names.note: English name from the article title; fr and de from Wikidata labels (P1843 entries: daim européen, Damhirsch).

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005). The species article also reports IUCN least concern.

range.note: native TR: the species article says Turkey is the only country with definitively natural populations since the Last Glacial Maximum. The article also says Italy, the Balkans and Rhodes are possibly native and that IUCN maps them as native; those are not listed here. Introduced AU: Australia section of the species article (Tasmania 1830, mainland 1880s; all jurisdictions except WA and NT); Wikidata distribution claim for AU is GRIIS, introduced. invasive_in AU: the article calls the deer a feral pest species in New South Wales. GBIF and Wikidata also list most European countries as introduced, and this record does not include them; see the PR.

traits.body_plan.note: Mammal with four legs; the genus article gives the taxon.

traits.limb_count.note: Cervid with four legs; the genus article describes the species as a deer and does not state the leg count.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Article: agile and fast; runs at up to 50 km/h over short distances; jumps up to 1.75 m. Walk is the foraging gait in the program. The article does not describe a trot or swimming, so neither is declared.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Mammal; the article does not state it directly. Standard for Cervidae.

traits.skin.note: Coat described in the species article (summer reddish with white spots, winter grey).

traits.flight.note: Not a flying animal; the article gives no flight.

traits.respiration.note: Mammal; lungs. Authored from the class, not stated in a source.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Mammal; no metamorphosis. Authored from the class.

traits.perching.note: Ungulate that does not perch. Authored.

traits.mass_kg.note: PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 57224.61 converted to kg. The article gives sex-specific typical masses (bucks 60-100 kg, does 30-50 kg); the PanTHERIA mean is consistent with them.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Lowest typical doe (30 kg) to highest typical buck (100 kg), from the article's sex-specific ranges.

traits.length_m.note: Average of buck midpoint (150 cm) and doe midpoint (140 cm), from the article. The article does not say whether 'long' means nose to tail or body only, so the measurement convention is unconfirmed.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Average of buck midpoint (90 cm) and doe midpoint (80 cm).

traits.lifespan_y.note: UNRESOLVED. The article says 'Their lifespan is around 12-16 years' without saying whether that is typical wild lifespan or a maximum or captive figure. The midpoint, 14, is a placeholder pending a source that states typical wild lifespan. Searches found only male-mortality and park studies, not open-licensed typical wild lifespans. Do not rely on this value without review.

traits.home_range_ha.note: PanTHERIA HomeRange_km2 0.71 converted to hectares (71 ha). PanTHERIA gives a mean across studies; the article gives no home range.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation from the New Forest study summarised in the article: grass in spring and summer, acorns and other mast from September to late December, shrubs and browse in winter. The article gives no percentages, so the shares (graze 0.5, browse 0.3, mast 0.2) are judgement. The source does not give percentages; the mast share is concentrated in autumn.

traits.social.note: Sexes are separated for most of the year; herds reach up to 150 before the rut; the smallest groups are females with fawns. The lower bound of 2 is authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: PanTHERIA ActivityCycle code 2 (crepuscular). The article gives no diel pattern. Activity is an authored proxy.

traits.defense.note: The article says the species is agile and fast when in danger, so flight is the main response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement. Parkland deer are tolerant of people, but wild herds flee.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: The article gives the preferred habitat as mixed woodland and open grassland. Resting in shrub cover is authored.

habitat.resources.note: Resource tags follow the diet allocation: graze for grass, browse for shrubs, mast for acorns in autumn (months 9-12), and shrub cover for shelter.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: The article mentions parks and woods used by deer near people (Phoenix Park, Epping Forest). The Adapter category is a judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: Authored: the article describes no hibernation, dormancy or migration. Herds stay in range.

seasonal.phases.note: AU mating: the article gives April as the Southern Hemisphere rut start and 135 days as its length. TR mating: second half of October in the Northern Hemisphere. AU young: derived from PanTHERIA gestation 230 days, not from an observed birth date.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Fawns are born in spring at about 30 cm and 3-4 kg. Juvenile scale 0.5 is authored.

vocalizations.note: Male groans described in the article. Context 'Song' is the nearest enum value; season, time window and cooldown are authored.

look.note: Colours from the article's description of the summer chestnut coat with white spots and the pale rump edged with black; proportions and the rump patch are authored. Antlers are not modelled; the article says only bucks carry them.

behavior.note: The shared ground-forager program was chosen as the closest fit for a ground-dwelling grazer. Parameters are authored. The program has no grazing-herd, rut, antler or swimming actions; food_tag graze and forage_gait walk follow the diet; flee_m, calm_m and food_m are judgement values.
